Date: 2026-09-24
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes

summary: Intro + objectives: Eden wants a multi-tenant throttling strategy using org and project keys, with predictable billing and a pilot on hosted Redwood. Walked through API key namespaces, quota slicing, sticky routing, and console demos (policy editor, usage dashboards). Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, KV prefix caching, and SSO/KMS requirements. Agreed next steps: share playbook, run benchmarks, gather traffic samples, security follow-up.
topics: Introductions; Current stack & constraints; Org vs project keying patterns; Quota slicing and fairburst; Sticky routing & backpressure; Console demo: policy editor and rate analytics; Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, cache); Security and compliance; Pilot proposal & next steps.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Meyers from Redwood, and with me are Emily and Samir on the SE side. Quick goals today are to show patterns for multi-tenant rate controls using org and project keys and to get to a pilot plan. Alex, Priya, Marcus — thanks for taking the time.

[00:28] Alex (Eden): Yeah thanks. We've been seeing token storms from a couple of internal teams and third-party partners. We need a way to isolate noisy tenants and protect our core checkout flows. We're also evaluating whether to go hosted first or bring you on Dedicated.

[00:45] Emily (SE): Totally. We'll start with the API model — how keys map to org > project and how quota slicing works — then jump into the Console to show live policy editor and quota dashboards. Expect some rough auto-transcript bits, sorry in advance if names get mangled.

[01:12] Priya (SRE): A quick note on constraints — we need 99.95% availability for the checkout path and <60ms p50 for embeddings calls. We also want audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and HSM-backed keys for secrets.

[01:35] Samir (SE): Good call. On availability, with Hosted you get SLAs and fallback policies; with Dedicated you get reserved GPU capacity and control plane isolation. For latency, we recommend pinning model variants and enabling KV cache for common prefixes — we'll demo the cache hit heatmap in the Console.

[02:10] Marcus (Product): Can you explain the org vs project keying patterns? We have org-level keys used by partners and project-level keys for internal apps. We want separate billing and quotas.

[02:30] Emily (SE): Absolutely. Pattern 1: 'Org-heavy' — org key maps to an account with per-org quotas and then project keys are child tokens with their own soft quotas. Pattern 2: 'Project-isolated' — each project is treated as a first-class tenant, easier for capacity slicing. Each approach affects billing granularity and routing. Sticky routing uses key metadata so requests consistently hit the same pool when needed.

[03:05] Jordan (AE): For Eden, given partner traffic, I'd suggest org-level billing + project tokens for partners. That gives you unified invoicing and the ability to throttle partners individually.

[03:38] Alex (Eden): How do you enforce burst limits? We can't have a partner spike kill the checkout.

[03:45] Samir (SE): We use a hybrid leaky-bucket + fairburst allocator. There's a per-key concurrency cap and a per-org overall throughput slice. If a partner exceeds their burst, requests hit backpressure and can be retried with exponential backoff. We showed a demo of the 'burst guard' in the policy editor — it'll be in the recording.

[04:20] Priya (SRE): Is backpressure client-visible as 429s or do you provide soft-queued responses?

[04:29] Emily (SE): Configurable. You can return 429s immediately or enable adaptive queuing which returns a token and a retry-after. We also support sticky fallback to a cheaper model variant during heavy load to keep critical flows alive.

[05:10] Marcus (Product): Walk me through how we'd set quotas per environment (prod vs staging). We want staging teams to have bigger dev windows but not impact prod.

[05:25] Samir (SE): In the Console you can create project-level policies tied to environment labels. e.g., project:checkout -> prod quota 1M tokens/day; staging project:checkout-stg -> quota 50k tokens/day. Policies can be inherited from org defaults. We demoed inheritance and override in the policy UI.

[06:15] Jordan (AE): I'm going to share a pattern doc after the call — it's the org/project keying playbook with recommended quota templates for fintech/retail.

[06:35] Alex (Eden): What about cost visibility? We need token-level cost breakdown per project and endpoint.

[06:44] Emily (SE): Redwood Console shows token, model, and route-level cost attribution. You can export CSVs and hook into billing APIs. For pilot, we can instrument top endpoints and show per-route cost.

[07:20] Jordan (AE): Now I'll hand over to Emily for the Console demo — showing policy editor, rate charts, and the Optimize suggestions pane.

[07:30] Emily (SE): (screen) Ok, here's the Console. Top-left is org selector, then project list. I'll open the policy editor for 'partners' — you can see default rate lane, concurrency cap, and a fairburst window. Notice the 'sticky routing' toggle and fallback model variant options.

[08:05] Emily (SE): A note: KV cache is labeled in the UI as 'prefix cache' — sometimes the transcript shows it as KV cash — it's cache, not cash — sorry. You can configure prefix TTL and max entries and get a hit-rate chart. Most customers see big cost wins on instruction-heavy prompt reuse.

[08:45] Priya (SRE): Can we set cache to be project-scoped? We can't allow partner prompts to be shared across projects.

[08:55] Emily (SE): Yes, caches are namespaced by project key by default. You can also enable cross-project cache for internal infra if you want, but default is isolated.

[09:20] Alex (Eden): How do rollouts look? We want canary for model upgrades.

[09:27] Samir (SE): Rollouts are in Console — configure percent traffic to new variant, set automatic rollback on quality/regression alerts. Redwood Optimize integrates with your eval-set to surface regressions.

[10:05] Marcus (Product): Speaking of Optimize, what does it recommend for high-qps chat vs embeddings workloads?

[10:14] Emily (SE): For chat you usually want smaller batch sizes but aggressive KV caching and prefix reuse. For embeddings we recommend larger batching and lower-precision quantized variants. The Optimize tool will suggest batching window and quantization profiles based on observed sequence lengths.

[11:02] Hannah (Security): A few security items: we require HSM-backed KMS for keys, SAML SSO, and audit log export. Do you support per-request encryption or bringing your own key?

[11:20] Samir (SE): We support KMS integrations and BYOK with HSMs for Private deployments. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption + customer-managed KMS for keys. Audit logs can be exported to S3 or pushed to your SIEM via secure connectors. We'll include our SOC2 pack in the follow-up.

[12:05] Priya (SRE): Any network constraints with Dedicated — do we need to open many outbound ports?

[12:15] Emily (SE): Dedicated can be deployed in a VPC with private subnets. The control plane talks over a single egress to our management endpoints; the data plane is customer-owned if you want on-prem. We'll share network diagrams in the security doc.

[12:55] Jordan (AE): Quick commercial note: pilot pricing is usually a month of reserved min capacity plus usage. I'll attach a sample SKU sheet.

[13:12] Alex (Eden): For partner stories, can we have different billing SKUs per partner under same org?

[13:20] Jordan (AE): Yes — you can map partner projects to different billing codes and export itemized invoices per project.

[13:38] Emily (SE): Back to policy examples — here's an example JSON policy we import: { /* elided in transcript */ } — the important bits are priority lanes, concurrency, burst-window ms, and model-fallback chain.

[14:05] Marcus (Product): Do you have built-in simulators for traffic shaping so we can model SLA impacts?

[14:12] Samir (SE): We have a simulation tool in the Optimize suite that can run traffic shapes and simulate how policies will throttle or route. We can run your traffic shape against our model and give an SLO hit report.

[15:00] Priya (SRE): For our pilot, we plan to run a partner-facing checkout flow and measure p95 latency. What's a reasonable batch config to start with?

[15:09] Emily (SE): Start with small batching — 25ms window for chat-y workloads — and enable KV cache for repeated prompts. For embeddings, batch up to 256 in a single request depending on sequence length. We'll fine-tune in the benchmark.

[16:20] Alex (Eden): We also need tenant segmentation for debugging — correlate traces to project key.

[16:28] Samir (SE): Trace ID includes project key metadata; Console has per-key trace viewer and you can hook into our tracing API to push to your APM.

[17:05] Jordan (AE): Let's touch on failure modes — if a heavy partner exceeds quota and we route to fallback cheaper model, do we still log full outputs for compliance?

[17:18] Hannah (Security): We need retention windows and proof that data doesn't leak between tenants.

[17:30] Emily (SE): Data separation is enforced at the ingress layer; project-scoped caches and storage ensure no crossover. Retention is configurable per org, and we provide audit logs for deletions. We'll send the retention matrix.

[18:05] Alex (Eden): Can you show how to create a quota slice for an org and carve out guaranteed capacity for checkout?

[18:12] Emily (SE): (screen) In policy editor — create a 'capacity slice' named checkout-guarantee -> guaranteed tokens/hour 15k -> priority lane: high -> fallback: model-small. Then assign to project:checkout. You can set sticky routing to ensure same pool.

[19:00] Marcus (Product): What happens if guaranteed capacity is exhausted?

[19:06] Samir (SE): Requests hit backpressure and are either queued (if adaptive queuing enabled) or rejected; you can set a graceful degradation policy to route non-critical calls to a cheaper model.

[19:40] Jordan (AE): We're about halfway — any urgent questions before we go deeper on the Optimize pane?

[19:48] Priya (SRE): One more — how do you handle partner keys when a partner is revoked mid-flight?

[19:55] Emily (SE): Revoke is immediate; we support token revocation APIs and can invalidate caches for that key. There's an option for 'soft revoke' to allow in-flight ops to finish.

[20:30] Emily (SE): Optimize pane — it surfaced a suggestion: reduce model variant for low-priority endpoints and enable a 50ms batching window for low-latency embeddings. It calculates estimated cost savings and expected latency delta.

[21:05] Alex (Eden): Can Optimize talk to our eval sets? We have a set of checkout prompts we want to keep regression-free.

[21:12] Samir (SE): Yes, you can upload eval sets; Optimize will run regression checks on rollouts and flag quality drops tied to prompts.

[22:00] Jordan (AE): Quick demo links and docs I'll share: rate-playbook, console-policy-examples, dedicated-network-diagram, SOC2-pack.

[22:20] Marcus (Product): Great. For the pilot success criteria: keep checkout p95 below 200ms, no single partner causes >10% p95 inflation, and billing visibility per project.

[22:45] Jordan (AE): Noted. We'll propose pilot SLOs and a 4-week plan.

[23:10] Hannah (Security): Please include the data flow diagrams and a short note on BYOK for Hosted.

[23:22] Emily (SE): Will do. Also note some auto-transcribed words may be slightly off — e.g., we sometimes see "KV cash" in the transcript. That's cache.

[24:00] Alex (Eden): Last item — can we temporarily bump a partner's quota for a marketing spike?

[24:08] Samir (SE): Yes, you can create an override policy or use the console to issue one-off bursts; there's a 'one-off grant' button for that exact scenario.

[25:00] Jordan (AE): OK, wrapping up — next steps and owners as we discussed. We'll schedule the benchmark run and security follow-up.

[25:20] Alex (Eden): Thanks everyone.

[25:25] Emily (SE): Thanks, we'll follow up with notes and links.

[25:30] (end of recorded transcript — remaining part of call used for quick Q&A and scheduling, short offline discussion recorded but not transcribed in full)
